motor.value: 84 W, 0.7 A, 120 V, 60 Hz; Singer claims '60% stronger than a standard sewing machine motor'

presserFootLift.value: Extra high presser foot lifter (manual: two-step lifter); no height published

threadTrimmer.value: Manual side cutter; no automatic cutter

includedFeet.value: General purpose foot, zipper foot, buttonhole foot, button sewing foot, edge and quilting guide, pack of needles, Class 15 transparent bobbins, spool caps, auxiliary spool pin; no walking foot (an even feed foot is optional per the manual)

warrantyUs.value: 25 yr limited on machine head, 2 yr on motor, light, wiring, switches, speed control and electronics, 90 days on adjustments, belts, rings, bulbs and attachments

conflicts: Motor claims: Singer's highlights say '50% more power' while its specification list says 'high-performance motor ... 60% stronger'; both are Singer marketing claims, neither names a baseline, and they do not agree with each other.
Throat: Singer gives 6.25 in as 'needle to tower', not needle to body, so it is not comparable to our throat figures and throatIn stays [verify].
Warranty: Singer's coverage page lists the 4432 Heavy Duty under Limited 25/2/90 Day, while the product page shows 90 day, 2 yr and 24 yr; 24 years against 25 is unresolved.
Weight: Singer's product page gives 14.6 lb, while an earlier Amazon-derived snippet showed 17.42 lb, likely a shipping weight; we use Singer's figure.
Dimensions: Singer's product page gives 15.5 x 6.25 x 12 in, while an earlier Amazon-derived snippet showed 15.2 x 12 x 6.2 in; we use Singer's figure.

Price: on 2026-10-01 Amazon showed $199.99 on the grey listing and $239.99 on the black (Sterling) listing, Singer's own price was $239.99 and its MSRP $299.99; the strike-through MSRP is a comparison price, not a selling price.
Stitch count: some forum commenters say the 4452 has more stitches than the 4432, but Singer's own pages list the same 32 built-in stitches and 110 applications for both; the 4452 differs by bundle.

price.priceSeenAt: Amazon, grey listing (the black and Sterling listings showed $239.99; Singer's own price $239.99, MSRP $299.99)

editorial.verdict: Singer's 32-stitch mechanical with a metal interior frame; owner reports on thick fabric and early defects are split, so buy it on price.
editorial.whoFor: Beginners who want more stretch and decorative stitches than the 4423's 23 and a one-step buttonhole, and who will mostly sew light to medium fabrics.
editorial.skipIf: You already know you want a walking foot or need to slow the machine down: the box has no walking foot and Singer's page says the 4532 adds speed control.
editorial.keySpec: 1,100 spm · 32 stitches · 1-step buttonhole · Class 15 top drop-in bobbin
strengths: Singer lists 1,100 spm, a metal interior frame, a stainless steel bed plate and a needle threader.
Owners report the metal frame holds up for the price, and several report it sewing multiple layers of canvas or denim.
Owners praise the one-step buttonhole and the range of utility stitches, and Class 15 bobbins are standard.
weaknesses: Owners report defects and setup problems often: bobbin winder, stitch selection stuck on straight stitch, buttonhole lever, though help threads over-represent problems.
Owners report tension and top-thread seating problems, and some re-thread before each use.
Owners report the machine runs fast with a touchy pedal, and Singer's page implies no speed control on the 4432 (it says the 4532 adds one).

checks.title: Which listing you are buying
checks.body: Amazon showed $199.99 on the grey listing and $239.99 on the black (Sterling) listing on 2026-10-01, and Singer's own price was $239.99 against an MSRP of $299.99. Amazon's 4.4 from about 11,960 ratings pools the grey, black and Sterling listings, so it is not specific to one.

checks.title: Price it against the 4452
checks.body: Singer lists the same 32 stitches for both. The 4452 adds a walking foot, non-stick foot, clearance plate and heavy duty needles for an MSRP $20 higher, so check the street gap before choosing the 4432.

checks.title: Test the basics on arrival
checks.body: Owners report stitch selection, buttonhole lever and bobbin winder faults on new units. Check the stitch dial, buttonhole and bobbin winding in the return window.

realCost: Walking foot: not in the box; the manual lists an even feed foot as optional, and the 4452 bundle includes a walking foot
Heavy duty needles for denim and canvas: the 4432 box has a pack of needles, and the 4452 bundle adds heavy duty needles

faqs.q: How many stitches does the Singer 4432 have?
faqs.a: Singer lists 32 built-in stitches and 110 stitch applications. The applications figure is a marketing count, not a stitch count.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Singer 4432 and 4452?
faqs.a: Singer's own pages list the same 32 stitches and 110 applications for both. The 4452 differs by bundle: it adds a walking foot, non-stick foot, clearance plate and heavy duty needles, at an MSRP of $319.99 against $299.99. Forum commenters who say the 4452 has more stitches are not supported by Singer's pages.

faqs.q: Is the Singer 4432 better than the 4423?
faqs.a: It has more stitches on paper: Singer lists 32 against 23 for the 4423, and an MSRP of $299.99 against $289.99. Whether that is worth it depends on the street price gap.

faqs.q: How does the 4432 compare with the 4411?
faqs.a: Singer lists the 4411 with 11 stitches and a four-step buttonhole, and no built-in needle threader. The 4432 has 32 stitches, a one-step buttonhole and a needle threader.

faqs.q: Does the Singer 4432 come with a walking foot?
faqs.a: No. The box has a general purpose, zipper, buttonhole and button sewing foot plus an edge and quilting guide. An even feed foot is listed as optional in the manual.

faqs.q: Can the Singer 4432 sew leather or canvas?
faqs.a: Singer markets it for projects 'from denim to canvas' and claims a motor '60% stronger' than standard, but those are its claims, and its highlights say '50% more power', a different figure with no baseline. Owner reports are split: some say it handles thick fabric and leather, others hand-turn the wheel through thick layers.

faqs.q: How much does the Singer 4432 weigh and how big is it?
faqs.a: Singer lists 14.6 lb and 15.5 x 6.25 x 12 in. An earlier Amazon-derived figure of 17.42 lb is likely a shipping weight.

faqs.q: What is the throat space of the Singer 4432?
faqs.a: Singer gives 6.25 in as 'needle to tower', not needle to body, so we do not list a throat figure and it shows as [verify].

faqs.q: What bobbins does the Singer 4432 use?
faqs.a: Class 15 transparent bobbins, loaded top drop-in.

faqs.q: Does the Singer 4432 have a speed control?
faqs.a: Singer does not state one for the 4432, and its page says the 4532 adds speed control. Owners report the machine running fast, with a touchy pedal.

faqs.q: What warranty does the Singer 4432 have?
faqs.a: Singer's coverage page lists it under Limited 25/2/90 Day, while its product page shows 90 day, 2 yr and 24 yr. The 24 against 25 years is a Singer discrepancy.
